source.title: Comparing Latent Concept Formation in State Space Models and Transformers via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Rithin Nagaraj; Rupa Laalasa Oruganti; Prerna Subhashchandra Kunder; Ashwini M. Joshi

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE feature analysis to real language models and reports cross-architecture alignment and a qualitative polysemanticity case relevant to the claim; it is an extension beyond the original toy-model setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports feature alignment, SAE-feature activation examples, and a Twin feature case study. Cited results from other work are not recorded. The Jaccard cutoffs are descriptive partitions, not independent findings about superposition.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool to compare Mamba-130m and Pythia-70m features by co-activation Jaccard. That tests universality, not superposition. No toy-model geometry, no neuron-spread measure, and no check that the SAE recovers true features. The 'polysemantic' Mamba unit is an SAE feature, not a neuron. It is attributed to the recurrent-state bottleneck, not to features competing for dimensions. It is also confounded by the smaller Mamba dictionary. No row measures what a version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim near-total feature alignment (99.98%) as preliminary support for the Universality Hypothesis, with divergence confined to structural/syntactic margins. They frame Mamba's polysemantic 'concept cramming' as a hypothesis from one Twin pair, needing symmetric SAEs. They argue qualitatively that its structured pattern points to architecture rather than dictionary size.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature dictionaries and binary co-activation Jaccard similarity across two language models, rather than toy networks and controlled feature-sparsity/importance sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors identify asymmetric SAE expansion factors (16 for Mamba and 64 for Pythia) as a confound; the alignment categories use empirically derived thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: 99.98% of Mamba-130m SAE features have max co-activation Jaccard >0.35 with some Pythia-70m SAE feature (range 0.234-0.412); no null baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Universality: SAE features in architecturally different LMs trained on similar data align at the feature level.

fits_no_version.finding: One Grey-Matter Mamba SAE feature (4454) fires on unrelated formatting contexts, while its Pythia twin fires only on table timestamps. The authors attribute this to Mamba's recurrent-state bottleneck, but it is confounded by the smaller Mamba SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A recurrent-state capacity bottleneck in SSMs produces polysemantic SAE features for rare syntactic/formatting patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: A few low-alignment Mamba SAE features fire on document-structure landmarks (External links headers, URL separators).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSMs learn architecture-specific structural landmark features absent in Transformers.

record.problems: The Pythia SAE is larger than the custom Mamba SAE, potentially affecting twin matching and Mamba polysemanticity. The proposed capacity mechanism rests on a qualitative single Twin feature case study and is not causally established. The Jaccard category thresholds are descriptive, and the paper notes the absence of a random-pair null distribution.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, or feature geometry.
No manipulation or measure of capacity, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared dimensions. The polysemantic unit is an SAE feature, not a neuron.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity not tested; only the dictionary-size confound is acknowledged.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no validation that SAE features recover the model's true features. SAEs are used, not tested.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features not tested. Cross-architecture matching is a different construct.

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies in the text: the diverging fraction is given as 0.02% and 0.03%. Feature 6888 (J=0.3415) is described among Grey Matter/Alien landmarks, implying the two Grey Matter features are 6888 and 4454. The text says Mamba 4454 also fires on table timestamps, but Table I shows no such Mamba context. The reader's V2 and V4 labels are dropped because no row measures what those versions name; the SAE is a tool here, not an object of test.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks or sparsity-dependent geometric transition are tested.
The study does not directly manipulate or quantify capacity pressure, test whether importance determines dedicated dimensions, or establish the mechanism across the Grey Matter distribution.
It does not test whether polysemanticity arises from causes other than capacity pressure.
It does not measure how many neurons each feature spans or independently validate feature recovery against a ground truth.
Completeness, stability, and canonicality of SAE features are not tested.
The dimensionality or direction geometry of the represented features is not tested.

rows.subject: Mamba-130m
rows.operation_detail: Measured each Mamba SAE feature's maximum binary co-activation Jaccard similarity to a Pythia SAE feature.
rows.measure: Distribution of maximum Jaccard similarities to Pythia features
rows.value: Global minimum 0.2343 and maximum 0.4116; 99.98% (12,285) had J > 0.35, 2 features (0.02%) had J ∈ [0.28, 0.35], and 1 feature (0.01%) had J < 0.25.
rows.note: Aggregate result across all 12,288 Mamba features. The paper says the thresholds are empirically derived descriptive partitions.
rows.check: Measures cross-architecture SAE feature alignment (universality), not superposition or SAE feature recovery. Max Jaccard tops out at 0.41 and there is no random-pair null, so 'strong alignment' has no baseline. The Pythia dictionary is 2.7x larger, which may inflate matching.

rows.subject: Mamba-130m, Feature 4454
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively inspected the activation context of the Mamba feature in the Twin Test.
rows.measure: Feature activation strength and activating context
rows.note: One of several distinct reported trigger types for the feature; the paper describes the feature as polysemantic.
rows.check: A single top-activating snippet for one SAE feature with no baseline. Polysemanticity of an SAE feature bears on dictionary quality and on an architecture-bottleneck hypothesis, not on V2's feature-importance/dimension-capacity account. The authors call it hypothesis-generating and confounded by the Mamba SAE's smaller expansion factor (16 vs 64).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports unrelated trigger contexts for Mamba Feature 4454 and a narrower timestamp trigger for its Pythia twin, consistent with the proposed cramming-versus-dedication pattern (R2-R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Single qualitative Twin feature case study
reader_labels.reason: The authors say the generality of the pattern across Grey Matter remains unknown and call the polysemanticity observation hypothesis-generating; the SAE dictionary sizes are also asymmetric (R2-R7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Mamba-130m and Pythia-70m-deduped on the stated Wikipedia corpus
reader_labels.reason: The study reports SAE feature dictionaries, strong cross-model feature alignment for 99.98% of Mamba features, and concrete feature activation examples (R1-R9).
